explanation: Markovnikov hydration: H⁺ adds to the less substituted carbon to make the more stable carbocation, water adds there and loses H⁺. Hydroboration–oxidation would put the OH on the other carbon. (Carey Table 16.1 example, 90%.)
tip: Dilute acid + water = hydration; concentrated acid + heat = the reverse (dehydration).
